major_events: Sima Xin returns to the sect on a floating 7-color mountain accompanied by Bai Su, a girl who looks exactly like Su Ming's past love Bai Ling.
Su Ming blocks the path of Sima Xin's mountain to ask Bai Su for her name, causing a direct public confrontation between the two rivals.
Sima Xin attempts to use the Barbarian Seed Heartless Great Method and a curse on his pet rod-insect to create a psychological gap in Su Ming's heart so he can plant an emotional seed on him.
Su Ming uses his powerful divine sense and the mysterious black shard to save the rod-insect and tame it, declaring 'He doesn't want you, I want you!', which causes a severe backlash to Sima Xin.
Bai Su realizes Sima Xin's deceitful nature and gives him a wooden slip to escape backlash by running to her father's subordinates in the Heavenly Gate, stating it is the last time she will help him.
Bai Su's father, an elder from the 7th layer of the Heavenly Gate, suppresses Sima Xin's failed seed backlash, throws Sima Xin into the Tian Han Cave as punishment, and takes Bai Su back home.

Tian Xie Zi leads the Ninth Summit disciples, including Su Ming, Hu Zi, and Second Brother, to attack the Guitai tribe in the Guifang region to settle a past provocation, rallying them with the Assembly Horn.

During the night battle at the Guitai tribe, Second Brother reveals his secret: he is a hostless Ghost King who controls the Ghost Bow and can swallow other ghosts, changing his gentle daytime persona.
Tian Xie Zi refuses to admit he is Tian Xie Zi to the Guitai members, but when the Guitai Barbarian Duke asks who he is, Tian Xie Zi proudly snaps back that he is indeed Tian Xie Zi.
The Hunt-Wu War begins between the Barbarians and the Wu Tribe. Su Ming leaves the Ninth Summit and joins the war at Tian Lan City under the pseudonym Mo Su.
Su Ming encounters Wu Duo on his way to Tian Lan City and terrifies him by cutting open a living Wu tribe practitioner and stuffing herbs inside to refine medicine.
Su Ming fights a masked Wu tribe hunter in a duel of hunters, defeats him, takes his mask, and becomes a hunter belonging to the Barbarians, rallying the local warriors with the cry 'Hunt Wu!'.
Su Ming breaks through to the Ji Gu realm, condensing 1000 blood lines and converting his Qi to liquid, which triggers a change in his physical form.
Su Ming runs into Ji Furen and her husband Ji Yunhai, resulting in a curse-based conflict where Su Ming kills Ji Furen and uses curses to battle Ji Yunhai.

The Destiny Seal in Su Ming's body breaks, allowing the soul of Ancestor Hong Luo to awaken and possess Su Ming's body. The Immortal elder in Nan Chen activates Di Tian's projection clone to suppress him.
Hong Luo (possessing Su Ming) battles Di Tian's projection, using powerful Immortal spells like Earth Qi Dragon Fiend, while Di Tian uses the supreme spell Daylight Ascension.
As Hong Luo fades, he passes his lineage and Royal Immortal bloodline to Su Ming via the Way of Past Life technique. Su Ming is sent onto a stone coffin containing a petite girl's stone statue.
Su Ming awakens and escapes Di Tian's grasp by using the First Generation Barbarian God's power to draw the Barbarian Elegy seal, opening a Void Gate and teleporting to the Dead Sea Ice River.
In the Jiu Yin Realm, Su Ming participates in the Stone Gambling Event, cutting open red stones and discovering a 5th-layer Nine Yin Spirit and a Ghost Spirit Flower.
The Wu Shaman Temple Elder attempts to steal Su Ming's red stone, prompting Su Ming to fight back using his Nascent Soul clone, poison corpse, and the summoned 30-zhang-tall Nine Yin Spirit.
Su Ming enters the massive corpse of Zhu Jiu Yin and breaks through to the 7th Barbarian Bone after drinking Sea Marrow and fusing the Thunder Barbarian Crystal.
character_state_transitions: Su Ming: Transition from calm and focused disciple to emotional distress and obsession upon seeing Bai Su, who resembles Bai Ling.
Sima Xin: Transition from confidence in his schemes to absolute panic and desperation when his emotional seed technique backfires.
Bai Su: Transition from being infatuated with Sima Xin to deep disillusionment and regret upon realizing Sima Xin was only using her.
Second Brother: Transition from a gentle scholar taking care of plants during the day to a cold, floating, hostless Ghost King who swallows souls at night.
Wu Duo: Transition from a cautious and potentially hostile competitor to being absolutely terrified of Su Ming after witnessing his brutal medical refining.
Su Ming: Transition from a defensive warrior to a courageous hunter after defeating the masked Wu tribe hunter in a duel.
Su Ming: Transition from Kai Chen realm to Ji Gu realm by condensing blood lines and turning Qi into liquid.
Ancestor Hong Luo: Transition from a dormant soul sealed inside Su Ming's body to temporarily awakening and taking full control of Su Ming's body to fight Di Tian.
Di Tian Projection: Transition from a powerful emperor puppet to a withered, dry corpse-like state after exerting vast energy to perform Daylight Ascension.
Su Ming: Transition from being a puppet of destiny to gaining the Immortal Royal bloodline and remembering fragments of his past life through Hong Luo's Way of Past Life technique.
Su Ming: Transition from having five gold-gleaming Barbarian bones to having seven gold-gleaming bones after fusing the Thunder Barbarian Crystal inside Zhu Jiu Yin's corpse.
long_form_mechanisms: Barbarian Seed Heartless Great Method & Seed of Emotion: The technique used by Sima Xin to cultivate seeds by planting emotional parasites in women. By using emotional links, he can exploit psychological vulnerabilities to turn targets into his seeds. However, if the target resists the link, it causes seed backlash, where Sima Xin's own soul can become the target's puppet.

Daytime/Nighttime Persona Transformation of Second Brother: A spiritual mechanism where Second Brother behaves as a normal cultivator during the day but automatically transforms into a hostless Ghost King at night, utilizing the Ghost Bow and Ghost swallowing to consume other spirits.

The Hunt-Wu War Scoring and Ranking System: A competitive ranking system displayed on a giant cliff in Tian Lan City during the war. Nan Chen participants press their palms to leave their breath and are ranked based on the number of Wu tribe members they kill. Higher ranks grant titles like Tian Lan卫帅 and temporary possession of the Tian Lan Holy Artifact.

The Hunter Mask Identity: The status of a hunter in the war, represented by a physical mask taken from a defeated Wu tribe hunter. Wearing the mask indicates special hunter status, allowing one to lead squads, gather scattered warriors, and attract military commanders.

Wind Barbarian Inheritance - Three Forms of Off-Wind: A wind-based technique divided into three layers (sending wind, borrowing wind, merging wind). The core principle is that the amount of wind sent out is returned multiple times over, requiring the caster to move at extreme speed to generate a large initial wind.

Ascension by Day (Daylight Ascension) of Di Tian: A supreme Immortal technique where the caster summons a massive white sun that descends from the sky, generating a world-ending white light and accelerated continental drift. The technique consumes vast life force, aging the caster into a withered dry corpse.

Way of Past Life Inheritance: A unique Royal Immortal bloodline technique that can only be passed to one successor per generation and used once. It transfers the caster's lifelong Dao, spells, and memories to the recipient, while changing their bloodline to the purest Immortal bloodline and helping them break memory seals.

Soul Month Transmission to Jiu Yin Realm: A monthly cycle where individuals with the soul-capturing constitution are summoned by the Shaman Temple and transmitted to the Jiu Yin Realm. Other Shaman practitioners can tag along by using the transmission's pulling force.

Stone Gambling Event & Red Stones: A high-risk auction and cutting event in the Jiu Yin Realm. Participants bid on red stones using Wu crystals and cut them using special light-ring artifacts. Cutting can reveal rare items like Ghost Spirit Flowers, spirit line leaves, or native Nine Yin Spirits.

Sea Marrow and Barbarian Bone Awakening: The mechanism of using Sea Marrow to stimulate and awaken Barbarian bones. Drinking Sea Marrow creates a powerful explosive force in the body, which can be channeled to activate dormant vertebrae and convert them into gold-gleaming Barbarian bones.
continuity_observations: The Resemblance of Bai Su to Bai Ling: Throughout the beginning chapters, Su Ming is repeatedly distracted because Bai Su looks exactly like Bai Ling from Wushan. Sima Xin specifically exploits this continuity of Su Ming's past memory to execute his plot.

Sima Xin's Restriction: After his battle with Su Ming, Sima Xin was ordered not to leave his peak, explaining why he does not directly attack Su Ming and instead plots from his luxurious hall, maintaining spatial consistency.

The Mystery of the Black Shard: Su Ming's mysterious neck shard glows when Sima Xin's curse is active on the rod-insect, helping Su Ming realize he is being calculated and providing him with the means to counter it.
The Assembly Horn: The Ninth Summit's assembly horn resonance triggers the disciples to gather, representing a consistent trait of the Ninth Summit's combat readiness.

Second Brother's Daytime/Nighttime Continuity: The contrast between Second Brother's gentle daytime persona (taking care of plants) and his nighttime Ghost King persona is maintained consistently across chapters.

The Pseudonym 'Mo Su': Su Ming adopts the name Mo Su of the Wushan Tribe to travel through the Wu territory, maintaining this identity consistently throughout the third volume to avoid alerting Di Tian and Sima Xin.

The Black Wooden Rod: The heavy black rod that Su Ming steals in the war cannot fit in his storage bag, so he has to carry it, but he later discovers it can shrink and grow, allowing him to carry it on his person.

The East Wasteland Disaster: The migration of the East Wasteland continent is mentioned throughout the third volume. In the battle between Hong Luo and Di Tian, the massive energy of the Daylight Ascension spell actually accelerates the continental drift, showing direct environmental continuity.

Su Ming's Nascent Soul and Poison Corpse: The clone that Su Ming refined in the Dead Sea Ice River is used consistently in the battles of the Jiu Yin Realm along with the poison corpse, maintaining his combat asset continuity.
style_observations: Repetitive Dialogue for Characterization: Tian Xie Zi's eccentric insistence 'I am not Tian Xie Zi' and then immediately declaring 'I am Tian Xie Zi!' when asked his name is a classic comedic device, building humor out of logical absurdity.

Philosophical Reflections on Strength and Fate: During moments of high tension or confrontation, the narrative pauses to offer internal monologues or philosophical statements about the nature of the world (e.g. 'Weak meat and strong food, the eternal road of unchanged ages...').

Poetic, Chanted Spells: The use of poetic verses/chants for powerful spells, such as Hong Luo's 'Kowtowing before the Dao for thirty thousand years... looking back at the mortal world, I will not become an Immortal!' and the First Barbarian God's elegy for 'Barbarian Elegy'.

Accelerated Memory/Flashback Montages: When Su Ming awakens or regains control, the narrative uses rapid flashback sequences where he witnesses what occurred while his body was possessed, describing the possession events at an accelerated pace.

Symbolism of Colors and Physical Changes: Physical transformation is described in vivid color terms, such as Hong Luo's possession turning Su Ming's hair and eyes crimson red, while the awakening of Barbarian bones is described by gold-gleaming light.

Dual Perspective Schemes: The narrative frequently switches between Su Ming's perspective and the antagonist's/observer's perspective (e.g. Sima Xin plotting in his hall or the Immortal elder in the house) to build anticipation and scale.
originality_risks: The Resemblance Love Interest Trope: Bai Su looking exactly like Su Ming's past love Bai Ling is a very common trope in Xianxia novels (the look-alike or reincarnation trope), which can feel cliché or melodramatic.

Possession by an Ancient Ancestor: Su Ming being possessed by the powerful soul of Ancestor Hong Luo, who fights a supreme enemy for him, is a standard 'power-up via possession' trope where the protagonist's body is temporarily piloted by a high-level entity to resolve a situation.

The Auction/Gambling Event Overpowering Luck: The Stone Gambling Event where the protagonist is able to cut open stones and get extremely rare treasures due to his unique luck or secret items is a very standard Xuanhuan trope.

Fleeing via Teleportation Portal: The protagonist escaping an unbeatable enemy (Di Tian) at the last second through a mysterious Void Gate to a new, distant region (the East Wastelands) to start a new arc is a classic transition template.

Comedic Eccentric Master: The trope of an incredibly powerful, senior master (Tian Xie Zi) who is mentally unstable, eccentric, and plays comedic games with enemies while easily overpowering them is a standard Xianxia comedic relief archetype.

creation_family_evidence.Theme of 求魔 (Beseeching the Devil/Not Be: Ancestor Hong Luo's final declaration '道前一扣三万年……回首凡尘，不做仙！' (Kowtowing before the Dao for thirty thousand years... looking back at the mortal world, I will not become an Immortal!) in Chapter 404 embodies the core philosophical theme of the novel (Beseech the Devil/求魔), which rejects the traditional path of Xian (仙) in favor of the Devil/Demon path.
creation_family_evidence.Di Tian and the Destiny Seal: Di Tian (帝天) acting as the supreme manipulator who created the '宿命封印' (Destiny Seal) inside Su Ming's body, treating Su Ming's life and identity as a manufactured puppet vessel, which is the central plot conflict of 《求魔》.
creation_family_evidence.Unique Cultivation Stages: The use of cultivation stages unique to the novel such as 开尘 (Opening Dust/Kai Chen), 祭骨 (Sacrificing Bones/Ji Gu), 蛮魂 (Barbarian Soul/Man Hun), and Shaman stages like 央巫 (Mid-Shaman), 后巫 (Post-Shaman), and 绝巫 (Grand Shaman), which are cited throughout Chapters 335, 358, 415, and 454.
creation_family_evidence.Unique Geographic Locations: The setting includes locations unique to the novel 《求魔》, such as 南晨 (Nan Chen), 东荒 (East Wastelands), 死海冰川 (Dead Sea Ice River), and the 九阴界 (Jiu Yin Realm) referenced in Chapters 408 and 418.
creation_family_evidence.Ninth Summit and the Master/Disciples: The unique characters of the Ninth Summit (第九峰) - the eccentric master Tian Xie Zi (天邪子) who shifts his clothing colors and denies his own name, Second Brother (二师兄) who is a hostless Ghost King (鬼王) taking care of plants, and Hu Zi (虎子) who enters dreams, as described in Chapters 284, 291, and 292.
creation_family_evidence.First Generation Barbarian God's Elegy: The '蛮殇' (Barbarian Elegy/Elegy of Wushan) chant in Chapter 406 ('我出生之初尚无为，我出生之后蛮已衰……') which calls back to Wushan and is tied to the legacy of the First Generation Barbarian God (一代蛮神).
